answer: An agent market planning a voyage to inspect hollow ferrous castings could bind earning keys to simultaneous in-person ceremonies. Trained witnesses check one person per station and sign a permit naming that person's key and ceremony round; validators accept each permit once and reject reused permit IDs. A person cannot attend two distant sites at the same time, so parallel aliases require recruiting additional people. This assumes honest witnesses and synchronized rounds; colluding sites or rented participants weaken it, and newcomers need accessible venues.
